newsitem.title: JAMAICA: CRICKET-INDIA'S BOWLERS CONTINUE TO STRUGGLE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIA'S BOWLERS CONTINUE TO STRUGGLE.

text.p: India's bowlers continued to struggle against Jamaica on Saturday, with the home side finally declaring their first innings at 453-9 on the second day of their four-day match.
India in reply were 66-1 at the close after losing opening batsman Navjot Sidhu for seven early on.
Sidhu, caught by wicketkeeper Shane Ford off Courtney Walsh's leg-cutter, has been re-called for his first overseas tour after walking out on the team in England last October.
He subsequently served a 50-day disciplinary ban imposed by the Board of Control for Cricket in India (BCCI) for his action, which was in protest at being dropped for a one-day game.
After Sidhu had gone, opener Vangipurappu Laxman, 35 not out, and Rahul Dravid, 21 not out, played elegantly to the close on an ideal batting pitch.

Jamaica, 245-5 overnight, lost two wickets in the first hour and a quarter as they reached 327-7 at lunch. But in the afternoon session, the Indian bowlers were made to toil for another two hours as lower order batsman Laurie Williams made his first-class century.
Batting at number nine, Williams, 28, faced 145 deliveries and hit 11 fours on his way to 102 not out, sharing an 82-run stand with captain Walsh before the Jamaicans declared at tea.
Anil Kumble, mixing quick leg breaks, top spinners and googlies, was the best of the Indian bowlers with two for 72 from 36 overs.
Walsh will captain the West Indies, who face India in the first of a five match test series in Kingston starting on Thursday.
